subject: Order form: carveouts for output ownership, training lockbox, and feedback license
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form: carveouts for output ownership, training lockbox, and feedback license

Team —

Attaching our first pass at redlines for Brightline (RI_redline_orderform_v1.pdf). Key commercial asks from the customer surfaced in last week’s demo: they want explicit productization rights for outputs, plus an ability to opt their data out of model training (they called it a "lockbox" or "no-retrain" flag). They also want a broad feedback license that would permit them to submit product improvements back to their own instance.

High level proposals we want legal to weigh in on:
- Output ownership: default to "customer owns output for their internal and productized use" but carve out examples where we need to reserve derivative rights (templates we ship, safety filters).
- Training lockbox: provide a contractual flag/attachment where customer can elect to exclude specific datasets from training for a defined period; technical enforcement via an ingestion tag + ops-only access.
- Feedback license: limited, non-exclusive license for feedback submitted through support channels to allow us to improve the service (we should propose limited use for diagnostics and safety but not for retraining customer models without opt-in).

Questions for legal/ops:
1) Are there standard RD/operations guardrails we can point to for the lockbox (retention, auditability, evidence)?
2) Does the feedback license language need a carveout for suggestions tied to customer confidential data?
3) Any appetite for a short-term escrow or attestation approach if legal pushes back on productization language?

Asks: Markus - can you run the attached PDF against Legal’s template? Priyom - can you note any ops/ticketing changes required for an opt-out flag? Laura - if you can prioritize, Brightline is asking to close by end of week.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form: carveouts for output ownership, training lockbox, and feedback license

Vivek —

Thanks for the draft; reviewed at a high level. Two quick legal notes before I run through the PDF with redline templates:

1) Output ownership: we can accept a customer ownership proposition for outputs used in their own product, but we need to clearly define "productize" vs "internal analytics". I suggest language that ties productization to "commercial distribution or public-facing product features" and reserves to Redwood the right to use aggregated, de-identified metrics for service improvement.

2) Training lockbox: acceptable in principle, but we need specifics on the scope (data types, time windows, access to snapshots). From an enforceability standpoint, an attachable schedule listing datasets + a technical flag will be the strongest approach. Ops will need a playbook for audits.

3) Feedback license: recommend we keep it limited — a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use feedback for service improvements, explicitly excluding customer confidential material and PII. If Brightline insists on a broader patent/derivative right, that will be an escalation.

Laura — can you draft redline snippets for (a) a productization definition, (b) a sample lockbox schedule clause, and (c) feedback license exclusions? Priyom — once I have the lockbox clause, we should map operational steps (ticket tags, retention checks, SOC evidence).

I'll push back on any language that would allow Brightline to force arbitrary retraining of core models.

-markus

From: Claire Park <c.park@brightline.com>

Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form: carveouts for output ownership, training lockbox, and feedback license

Vivek / team —

Thanks — we've reviewed and pushed a set of counter-redlines (attached: Brightline_redlines_v2.docx). A few clarifications from our side:

- On output ownership: Brightline needs explicit downstream rights so our engineering team can ship features that incorporate model-generated content to customers. That's a key purchasing condition for us. We are open to reasonable safeguards (no wholesale re-sale of the Redwood model), but we need a clean path to productization.

- On the lockbox: our security team is asking for both (a) contractual assurance and (b) an audit report capability that shows the excluded datasets were not used in any retraining for a 12-month period. They proposed an annual attestation from Redwood and a scoped SOC evidence packet.

- On feedback: we can accept a narrow license for diagnostics, but our product teams submit feature ideas through support tickets and we'd like a path for Redwood to accept feedback under an express, project-limited collaboration without claiming ownership.

We are available to do a call with legal and ops tomorrow afternoon. Are you able to provide a sample lockbox schedule (even a template) prior to the call?

Claire Park
Head of Partnerships
Brightline

Subject: Re: Order form: carveouts for output ownership, training lockbox, and feedback license

Claire —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and clear asks. Next steps:

1) Laura and Markus will finalize the sample lockbox clause + productization definition today and post the snippets to the Drive link. Expect a short carveout schedule template (training-lockbox-specs.xlsx) we can attach to the OF.
2) Priyom will scope the operational playbook for the opt-out flag and the evidence artifacts we can produce for an annual attestation.
3) I'll schedule a 45-minute legal/ops sync for Monday 10am PT (invitation to follow).

Regarding the attestation ask: we can provide an annual attestation and a scoped SOC evidence packet (logs, ingestion markers). We should confirm what Brightline needs from a granularity perspective (dataset-only? model-level?). If they want full model training pipeline artifacts, that will be out of scope for standard SaaS — we'll propose a scoped packet that is realistic to deliver.

Are you ok with Monday 10am PT for the call?

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
